about: T16.1 reader contract vectors. Consumed by reader-contract.test.ts and backend/reader/reader_contract_test.go. Not a parity claim: gaps are characterized, not normalized away. Per-method gap lists name the incompatibilities in the fields that frontend method actually populates (getFixtures and getLiveWindow do not enrich scorers or stats), not every field their shared reader route can return.

evidence.recorded: Unmodified recorded ESPN payloads under src/server/data/__fixtures__ (both languages read the same bytes).
evidence.synthetic: Synthetic, labeled where they appear: queries.events and queries.liveMinute, freshness snapshots, transport paths, summary.syntheticOverlay, standings.unnamedTable and standings.synthetic, player.missingContext, the reader match/bracket UUIDs, the integration test's standings tie rows and provisional team, and the seedLigaTeam standing behind team.readerStandingSummary. None is a production crosswalk.
evidence.crosswalk: Provider-to-canonical team ids come from the production seed (backend/config/teams.seed.json, exported to src/server/data/teamCrosswalk.json). Summary and own-goal side ids are checked against it in both suites; standings ids through the group-A comparisons (TS crosswalk, Go seed); bracket side ids only in the Go database suite.

T10.1-match-query.mismatch: Reader /matches ignores range/state/detail/limit (even malformed) and returns the whole season with 200; the frontend selects a window or returns 400.

T10.2-team-stats.mismatch: Reader TeamStats lacks passesAccurate/crossesAccurate/tacklesEffective and its accuracy percentages are ESPN's one-digit fractions x100 (40) instead of operand-derived values (35.7).

T10.2-lineups.mismatch: Reader lineups hold starters only (11 per side, 26 in the frontend) and LineupPlayer lacks starter/stats/athleteId/playerSlug, though each reader jersey URL still embeds the provider event and athlete ids.

T10.2-leaders-depth.mismatch: The frontend caps each leader board at 10 rows (TOP_SCORERS_SHOWN in store.ts); the reader's top-scorers SQL has no limit and serves every stored row (the ingester stores 30 per board, topScorerLimit).

T10.2-leaders.mismatch: Reader serves goals only as TopScorer{goals}; the frontend StatLeader uses value plus athleteId/teamId/playerSlug and an assists board. No assists route.

T10.3-team.mismatch: Reader TeamProfile lacks standing, scheduleAvailability and per-match scope (pinned in team-insights.json).

T10.3-squad.mismatch: No standalone squad route; the squad exists only inside TeamProfile.

T10.10-derived-standings.mismatch: Reader Group has no labelKey/zones and no Leagues Cup phase or MLS overall tables.

T16.6-news.mismatch: Reader news is a live ESPN proxy (502 on upstream failure), not owned data; bodies match today.

T17.3-freshness-coverage.mismatch: Standings, top-scorers and news responses carry no X-ScoreArc freshness headers.

T10.3-team-location.mismatch: Reader TeamProfile.location is always null (no column is selected); the frontend maps the provider location.

T10.3-squad-fields.mismatch: Reader SquadPlayer.id is a canonical player UUID, not the provider athlete id; age and headshotUrl are always null (no column is selected); and the squad is served in shirt-number order rather than provider roster order.

T10.3-partial-failure.mismatch: The frontend getTeam/getSquad degrade a failed roster or schedule to empty (squad [], schedule unavailable) and return null only when the profile fails; the reader fails the whole team request with 500 when any child query fails.

T10.3-standing-summary.mismatch: Reader standingSummary is generated as '<rank> in <competition id>' from the standing row; the frontend serves the provider's own string.

T21.4-dependency-error-logging.mismatch: Every reader data handler except handleTeam (matches, standings, bracket, top-scorers, news, match summary) logs the raw dependency error text, which can carry connection details; handleTeam logs only operation, error type and SQLSTATE.

T16.2-standings-dedup.mismatch: A team listed in two provider tables stays in both frontend tables; the reader keeps one standing row per team per season, so it lists the team only in its first table (the remaining rows of a later table keep their true positions). Representing multi-table membership needs an owner decision: a multi-table standing model (standing and standing_snapshot keys) or a shared first-table rule. No configured competition published overlapping tables on 2026-10-04.

T10.3-team-cache-doc.mismatch: handleTeam serves Cache-Control public, max-age=120, but OpenAPI documents the team route with StandardCacheControl (public, max-age=60).

T10.3-team-record.mismatch: The frontend TeamProfile.record is the provider's record item (summary string, gamesPlayed, points, goalDifference from provider stats); the reader derives W-D-L, games, points and goal difference from its own standing row.

syntheticOverlay.note: Synthetic: merged over the recorded 760490 summary because no recorded payload has a shootout or head-to-head block. Norway (away) is listed first to prove side mapping by id; six meetings prove the five-row cap; one string, one numeric and one missing score. An absent provider score renders as 0 in both implementations ('CIV 4-0 NOR'): characterized shared behavior that collapses missing into zero, not an endorsed contract. Appended key events add the second state of each discriminator (a penalty goal, a shootout kick, a red card). A goal and a card credited to provider team 999999, which is neither side, prove an unattributable reference: the frontend keeps the provider id, which matches neither of its sides, and the reader serves null rather than a default side; header shootoutScores give the reader's summary-side shootout aggregate.

transport.note: Frontend and reader envelopes and caching differ by design and are not interchangeable: the frontend routes are no-store proxies, the reader is a public CDN-cacheable API. Both are pinned here; choosing the cutover caching is apiStore work (T16.3), not a DTO gap.

shootoutPrecedence.note: Synthetic: recorded event 760489 (Germany 1-1 Paraguay, structured shootoutScore 3/4 and the note 'Paraguay advance 4-3 on penalties') with its shootout evidence replaced per case. 'absent' removes the field; a null note removes the notes. One precedence in both languages: summary header (where a summary is held) > scoreboard structured totals > anchored note > null. Regulation scores never change.
